#  23436 - Advanced Finite Element Methods Modulübersicht  
|  Module Number:   | **23436 - module is no longer offered from WS 2026/27**  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Module Title:  | **Advanced Finite Element Methods**  |  
|  Finite Elemente Methoden für Fortgeschrittene   |  
| Department:  |  Faculty 6 - Architecture, Civil Engineering and Urban Planning   |  
| Responsible Staff Member:  | 
  * Dr.-Ing. Firl, Matthias 

 |  
| Language of Teaching / Examination:  | English  |  
| Duration:  | 1 semester  |  
| Frequency of Offer:  |  Every semester   |  
| Credits:  |  
| Learning Outcome:  |  **Knowledge** Development, application and behaviour of specific, high performance finite elements**Application** Application of the Finite Element Method in Structural Engineering problems**Abilities** Critical evaluation of the Finite Element solution, working with the general purpose Finite Element program ANSYS  |  
| Contents:  | 
  * Linear, Straight Timoshenko Beam Element
  * Galerkin-weighted Residual and Variational Principles
  * “Standard” and “Hierarchical” Element Shape Functions
  * Shear Deformable Plate Element, Locking
  * Variational Formulation of Finite Elements
  * Alternative Finite Element Formulations
  * Error Estimation and Adaptivity

 |  
| Recommended Prerequisites:  | 11144 (MM1), 23427 (MM3)(This courses should be taken before or simultaneously with the module. A certificate is not required for the registration.)  |  
| Mandatory Prerequisites:  | None  |  
| Forms of Teaching and Proportion:  | 
  * Lecture / 4 Hours per Week per Semester 
  * Self organised studies / 120 Hours 

 |  
| Teaching Materials and Literature:  | 
  * Manuskript LS Statik und Dynamik, BTU Cottbus-Senftenberg
  * Zienkiewicz, O.G., Taylor, R.L., The Finite Element Method, Mc Graw Hill, 1989/91Vol. 1: Basic Formulation and linear ProblemsVol. 2: Solid and Fluid Mechanics, Dynamics and Nonlinearity
  * Cook, R.D. Concepts and Applications of Finite Element Analysis, J.Wiley, 1989
  * Werkle, H., Finite Elemente in der Baustatik, Vieweg, 2008
  * Bathe, K.-J., Finite Element Procedures in Engineering Analysis, Prentice Hall 1982

 |  
| Module Examination:  | Continuous Assessment (MCA)  |  
| Assessment Mode for Module Examination:  | 
  * Successful completion of 3 written documentations - as homework (60%)
  * Oral examination, 40 min. (40%)

 |  
| Evaluation of Module Examination:  | Performance Verification – graded  |  
| Limited Number of Participants:  | None  |  
| Part of the Study Programme:  | 
  * no assignment

 |  
| Remarks:  | SS3In the event that the module cannot be taught or tested according to the present description (e.g. for reasons of infection protection), the alternatives communicated on relevant platforms (e.g. homepage or Moodle) apply.  |  
| Module Components:  | 
  * Lecture/Seminar Advanced Finite Element Methods
  * Examination Advanced Finite Element Methods

 |  
| Components to be offered in the Current Semester:  | 
  * no assignment

 |  
| Follow-up Module/s:  |  Phase-out module since: 14.07.2015 
  * without Follow-up Module/s

 |
